metadata.case_name: HO SHUK MAN v. NORMAN WONG WAI NOK AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: tear of the supraspinatus tendon (rotator cuff); tendinosis changes; impingement syndrome; partial tear of the supraspinatus tendon
source: MRI demonstrated tear of the supraspinatus tendon (rotator cuff), sprain of acromioclavicular joint (“ACJ”) and bone contusion. The MRI showed mild increased signal intensity into the supraspinatus tendon compatible with tendinosis changes.
Both agreed that the cause of the pain in her right shoulder was impingement syndrome and tendinosis and partial tear of the supraspinatus tendon.

manifestations.description: intermittent and involuntary tremor of right upper limb
intermittent pain in right shoulder (5 to 6 episodes a day, each for 15-30 minutes)
cold sensation and no blood flow in fingers of right hand
swelling of right arm and hand after 30 minutes of inactivity of the limb
has to rely on left upper limb for activities of daily living like eating a piece of bread
intermittent pain in both wrists such that cannot carry more than 2 catties (about 1.2 kg) of vegetables
difficulty and decreased frequency of sexual intercourse since the accident
tend to stay away from friends, fear when facing crowds, poor mood and ill temper
residual pain on abduction especially to shoulder level
neck pain due to mild degeneration of the C4-C5 disc

treatments_received: physiotherapy (outpatient and courses up to February 2009 and restarted November 2009)
steroid injection to the subacromial bursa on 6 October 2007
admitted to Baptist Hospital for MRI
Arthroscopy of right shoulder (7 to 10 May 2008)
occupational therapy (up to March or April 2009)
